blocks.title: Not from your PDFs
blocks.text: Your PDFs do not cover this topic, so this page was written for the site. Your 12-week plan lists React, hooks, rendering, performance, state management and TypeScript. Check it against the official documentation, or give me a PDF to replace it.

blocks: Test what the user sees and does, not implementation details. A test that survives a refactor is worth more than one that checks internal state. Your Spring guides cover JUnit, Mockito and Testcontainers; these are the equivalents for the frontend.

walkthrough.title: A mock
walkthrough.text: `vi.fn()` plays the role of a Mockito mock.

walkthrough.title: Find by role
walkthrough.text: Query as a user would: by role and name. This also checks accessibility.

walkthrough.title: Assert the result
walkthrough.text: Check what happened, not the component's internal state.

walkthrough.title: queryBy for absence
walkthrough.text: `getBy` throws when nothing matches; `queryBy` returns null, so it can assert absence.

blocks.title: MSW intercepts fetch, so the component is unchanged
Gotcha
blocks.text: `getBy` fails immediately if the element is not there yet. After async work use `await findBy...`, which retries for a short time.

blocks.title: Interview angle
blocks.text: **How do you test a React component?** With React Testing Library: render it, interact as a user through roles and text, and assert what appears. Mock the network with MSW rather than mocking `fetch` or your hooks, so the test stays close to reality.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
- Test behaviour, not implementation.
- Prefer queries by role, then label, then text.
- Use `findBy` after async work, and `queryBy` to assert absence.
- Mock at the network with MSW.
- Keep a few end-to-end tests for critical journeys.

items.question: What is the difference between `getBy`, `queryBy` and `findBy`?
items.answer: `getBy` throws if missing, `queryBy` returns null if missing, and `findBy` returns a promise that retries until the element appears.

items.question: Why query by role rather than by CSS class?
items.answer: Roles reflect what the user perceives and survive styling changes, and they catch missing accessibility.

items.question: Why mock with MSW instead of mocking your API module?
items.answer: The real fetch code and error handling still run, so the test covers more and needs no change when you refactor the client.
